name: wincompat
description: WIN-MIN: a real Windows x64 console program (built with MinGW) runs on the OS through winrun -- parse, map+relocate, resolve imports, run, exit code -- and corrupt executables are refused

build.name: userspace
build.why: ships bin/winrun plus the Windows fixtures (needs mingw-w64 on the build host)

assertions.why: the parser is fed attacker-controlled files: ASAN/UBSAN unit tests + a 300k-iteration mutation fuzzer must pass on the host
the OS came up
the fixtures made it into the initrd (mingw-w64 present on the build host)
init ran every fixture to completion
no kernel fault while running foreign code

assertions.pattern: WINRUN: L0 parse OK file=/usr/share/winfix/nocrt_hello.exe .*machine=x86_64 subsystem=console image_base=0x140000000
assertions.why: the PE32+ header is validated and understood

assertions.pattern: WINRUN: L1 mapped at 0x[0-9a-f]+ preferred=0x140000000 delta=nonzero relocs=applied
assertions.why: the image was placed away from its preferred base and its relocations applied
all three kernel32 imports (GetStdHandle, WriteFile, ExitProcess) resolved to working functions
control was transferred through the Windows x64 ABI
the program's own text reached the console: proves WriteFile works AND that the pointer in .data (which needed a relocation) was fixed up correctly
ExitProcess(42) ended the process with exactly that code
the stages happened in the right order -- not just that each marker exists somewhere
a valid header cut short is refused (and the line names THAT file, so a read failure on a good file cannot satisfy this)
512 bytes that are not a PE are refused
a real PE whose Machine says ARM64 is refused
the VALID tier-1 program must not be refused by the parser/reader
a rejected file must never reach the entry point
refusing garbage must not hurt the kernel
an ordinary MinGW program parses and maps
MEASURES the remaining gap: the UCRT/msvcrt imports an ordinary program needs (printf, malloc, __getmainargs, ...). Turns green when tier 2 lands.

assertions.name: final
assertions.why: the desktop still painted while foreign code ran
